title: Stalk faithfulness for derived objects
statement:
A morphism in $D(T_{\Et})$ is an isomorphism if and only if its
pullback to every geometric point of $T$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: An isomorphism remains an isomorphism under every derived inverse-image functor. This gives the forward implication by Functor.map_isIso.

For the converse, apply DerivedCategory.isIso_iff to reduce to invertibility of H^q(alpha), for each integer q. For each point s of T, use t = T.algClosurePoint s, whose residue field is algebraically closed. By hypothesis the derived pullback of alpha along t is invertible, so its q-th homology map is invertible. The natural isomorphism Functor.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso for the exact inverse image identifies that map with t^*(H^q(alpha)); NatIso.isIso_map_iff transports invertibility. This uses the existing proved generic homology comparison, including naturality in alpha, rather than only an objectwise existence of comparison isomorphisms.

Apply the fibre functor at the identity geometric point of Spec Omega to the invertible map t^*(H^q(alpha)). The natural isomorphism upperStarCompUliftSheafFiberIso, specialized to t and the identity and simplified by identity composition, identifies the resulting map with the geometric fibre of H^q(alpha) at t. Thus every member of the canonical conservative family T.uliftPointSmallEtale sends H^q(alpha) to an isomorphism. Scheme.isIso_of_isIso_sheafFiber_map implies that H^q(alpha) is invertible. This completes the homology criterion, with no boundedness assumption.
